builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
summary: The method replaces sequential, single-pass large-model summarization of agent interaction histories with parallel drafting of structured summary slots by a fine-tuned small model, which the target model then verifies line-by-line and repairs where needed. Costs include training and maintaining the drafter model, additional system complexity for parallel generation and verification orchestration, and potential quality trade-offs that the paper notes are model- and task-dependent. The approach can fail when the small drafter produces low-quality slot proposals that the target model must extensively repair, reducing or negating speedup, or when downstream task performance degrades due to information loss from aggressive or inaccurate compaction.
rationale: SpecCompact offers a promising speedup for a known latency bottleneck in agent systems, but requires workload-specific validation because it involves fine-tuning a custom drafter and its quality-speed trade-off varies by model and task.
technique: Slot-parallel speculative verification for context compaction

claims.statement: The method replaces sequential, single-pass large-model summarization of agent interaction histories with parallel drafting of structured summary slots by a fine-tuned small model, which the target model then verifies line-by-line and repairs where needed. Costs include training and maintaining the drafter model, additional system complexity for parallel generation and verification orchestration, and potential quality trade-offs that the paper notes are model- and task-dependent. The approach can fail when the small drafter produces low-quality slot proposals that the target model must extensively repair, reducing or negating speedup, or when downstream task performance degrades due to information loss from aggressive or inaccurate compaction.
Achieves 2.04--5.63x compaction speedups over Hermes-style summarization across AppWorld and tau^3 benchmarks, with an 8.68x median speedup in a Hermes user study.
